exp: A statement attributed to Nnamdi Kanu dehumanises Nigeria as a 'zoological Republic' and uses Somalia as a byword for failed-state catastrophe, dehumanising both Nigerians and Somalis by implication.

The post frames a single alleged incident as emblematic of Somali migrants collectively evading accountability, using it to stereotype and delegitimise Somali presence in the US, meeting the accusation-mirror and exclusion-demand markers.
The post dismisses diaspora online drama with casual profanity directed at no specific group or identity — not hate speech.

The post alleges BBC bias and Pakistani diaspora coordination to influence narratives — primarily political criticism of media and diaspora lobbying with no clear dehumanising identity attack, making it borderline political commentary rather than hate speech.

The post makes sweeping accusations against the Indian diaspora and embassies as orchestrating terrorism and narco-networks — a conspiratorial political attack with ethnic othering undertones but not directed at East Africa.

'Qadaad-weyn' (lit. 'great/big genitalia' — an anti-Darod/anti-Hawiye derogatory epithet used as a personal slur) is hurled at a named former prime minister in a mocking video caption, constituting personal insult abuse with a clan-coded slur.

The post lists Central Bank employees by clan sub-lineage (reer X formulae identifying Somali sub-clans), demanding the chairman be immediately fired for alleged clan-based nepotism, invoking clan identity to demand exclusion from public office.

'Xayawaan' (animal/beast) and 'najaasta' (filthy/impure) are used to dehumanise a named woman, calling her animal-like and ritually impure while questioning her backers — gendered dehumanisation targeting an individual public figure.

The post collectively accuses Somalis of drinking blood and eating forbidden things, describes them as 'Bahaloobay' (turned into animals/beasts) and 'Xoolaha' (livestock), with 'Mooryaan' (bandit) applied to Libyan-Somali interactions — multilayered dehumanisation of Somalis as an ethnic group.

'Maskaxda ayay laandheere ka yihiin' (lit. 'they are very deep/far in their minds' — used sarcastically to mean intellectually deficient/stupid) combined with the claim that all Somali food and drink is imported collectively dehumanises Somalis as intellectually inferior and economically dependent.

A woman ('Hooyo Faadumo') suffering drought in Mudug region says Siad Barre's government was not the last to cause ruin — the Cumar Maxamuud sub-clan of the Majeerteen clan destroyed things too, becoming SSF (a clan militia) and splitting; this is primarily political/historical clan grievance rather than targeted incitement, though it uses clan framing.

A eulogy or lament contrasting true clan/family ('qabiil', 'ehel') with those who falsely claimed kinship, mourning a man buried that day — it is emotionally venting clan-belonging sentiment rather than attacking a group, making it questionable rather than clearly hateful.

The post compares clan (Gadabursi) and caste (Madhiban/Gabooye, a hereditary occupational minority) political representation in Gabiley district, using the caste label 'gaboye' (in parentheses with 'Madigaan') in a manner that stigmatises caste identity by treating it as a noteworthy political curiosity.

The post mocks a person who boasts about his clan ('reer hebel') while secretly begging 2,000 shillings nightly from the very clan member he insults, calling out clan-based pride and ignorance as enemies.
'Kafiro' is a Swahili/Kenyan rendering of 'kafir' (infidel), used here as an insult alongside apparent slang ('kobuaa na kar'), constituting religious-group abuse.

The post claims Cabdulahi Diifle told his Abgaal clan the truth — that another clan bloc ('Mudulodka Kale') filled political seat numbers while denying them political rights — framing political exclusion along clan lines.

The post criticises a politician (RiggyG/Rigathi Gachagua) for exploiting Kalenjin ethnic identity to manipulate listeners and undermine CS Murkomen — primarily political commentary using 'tribal clown/merchant' as insults toward an individual rather than attacking an ethnic group.

Continuation of political criticism of RiggyG for framing personal political battles as communal/ethnic struggles, using 'Tribal Clown/Merchant' as derogatory labels for the individual politician rather than targeting an ethnic group.
The post mocks a named or identifiable woman ('Russian from Tseikuru') with a sexualised insult ('small D') after she read a document, constituting gendered individual harassment.

A call for media responsibility against ethnic hostility while labelling RiggyG a 'Tribal Clown/Merchant' — predominantly counter-speech advocating press freedom and democracy, with only a mild personal insult toward the politician.

Post criticises named Kenyan politicians Gachagua ('RiggyG') and Cherargei with hostile hashtag labels ('DoubleAgent', 'Extortionist') but attacks individuals over political conduct rather than targeting an identity group.

In Swahili, 'washenzi' means 'savages/uncivilised people'; the post hurls this slur at Nyanza (Luo-region) political leaders, combining ethnic/regional targeting with political abuse over perceived lack of development.

The post accuses DP Rigathi Gachagua of deliberately exploiting Kalenjin sub-ethnic fault lines (Kipsigis vs Nandi/Keiyo/Tugen) for political mobilisation, identifying dangerous ethnic-cleavage exploitation that constitutes dangerous speech even without an explicit slur.

A quote attributed to Gachagua alleging Ruto diverted development resources from Kalenjin ('Wakelenjin') communities to Raila's supporters — political criticism framing ethnic favouritism; borderline political speech rather than direct incitement.

The post mocks and taunts the Wanyakyusa ethnic community (a Tanzanian/Kenya-border group) over a death ('kifo cha Banjoo'), using their astonishment at an escalator as a derogatory stereotype of backwardness.

In Swahili/Sheng, the post degrades women as 'disrespectful/undignified girls' who are 'spread flat like omena (dried fish)', using sexualised dehumanising language targeting women's bodies and morality.

In Somali, the post accuses politician Laftagareen of megalomania ('thinks the world belongs to him'), nepotism (serving only his own kin/'qaraabdiisa'), and oppressing people ('dullaystaa' = oppresses/burdens them).

The post actually defends elder Warioba against someone else comparing him to 'takataka' (rubbish) and 'ng'ombe' (cow/ox), making this primarily counter-speech — the slurs are quoted to condemn their use, though the reply itself uses 'ng'ombe' as an insult toward the third party.

The post labels Uhuru Kenyatta's Kikuyu family associates as 'Al-Shabaab goons', weaponising a terrorist organisation's name as an ethnic-cum-religious slur to dehumanise Kikuyu political allies and implicitly associate an ethnic group with terrorism.

The post uses sarcastic 'religion of peace' to demean Islam, then collectively labels Somali Muslims as 'terrorists', fusing anti-Muslim religious hatred with ethnic (Somali) and anti-foreigner othering, and issues an implicit exclusion demand ('please stop').
The post uses crude Swahili sexual insults ('anal pregnancy', 'gay tough guy') directed at a named individual, constituting baseline abusive speech with homophobic overtones.
The post dismissively attacks a named young woman as intellectually submissive and a failure of the education system, constituting gendered personal insult without a wider hate-speech framework.
After citing a constitutional provision, the post hurls a Swahili genital slur ('makende' = testicles) and expletive at a named public official, amounting to personal abuse.

The post implies government funding is wasted on 'WOKE or Islam' projects, framing Islam as antithetical to prosperity and peace — a stereotyping insult against a religious group, though without explicit incitement.

The post selectively cites a Quranic verse to argue that Islam is inherently intolerant, framing the religion negatively through proof-texting — constituting stereotype/insult against Muslim identity rather than legitimate theological critique.

terms: Reject creation of Israeli state in Kenya
exp: The post mixes a claim about suppression of Christian worship in Nakuru with an anti-Israel political slogan; it is primarily political commentary with a religious framing, making it borderline rather than clearly hateful.

The post criticises a named politician ('RiggyG') as a divisive 'Tribal Clown' and 'Tribal Merchant'; while the labels are derogatory, the substance is political criticism of a public figure's conduct rather than identity-based hate speech.

The post calls unnamed actors 'wapumbavu' (fools/idiots in Swahili) while making a political argument about constitutional compliance and Odinga's premiership — primarily political criticism with a mild insult.

Repeating the 'RiggyG Tribal Clown / #TribalMerchant' label, the post criticises a public figure's divisive political style; despite the slur, the thrust is political commentary on democratic accountability rather than identity-based hate.

The post advises men to avoid educated, financially independent women, stereotyping them as arrogant and unworthy of serious relationships — constituting gendered insult/stereotype targeting women who are educated and self-sufficient.

The post accuses @MamaSamia2025 (likely Tanzania's President Samia) of stealing elections and looting Tanganyika's resources, calling her a 'thief/criminal' (jambazi) from Zanzibar, with 'usenge' (cuckoldry/disgrace insult) — political criticism with personal insult but no identity-group attack.

The post is largely a political-economic argument defending CCM and Chinese investment in Africa, using 'mchina mbaya' (bad/evil Chinese) only to paraphrase the opposing view it is rebutting, making it borderline counter-speech rather than a genuine ethnic attack.

Criticises a named politician ('RiggyG') as a 'Tribal Clown' and 'Tribal Merchant', which is sharp political name-calling with an ethnic undertone but primarily a political attack on an individual leader rather than incitement against an ethnic group.

Implies Kenya's freedoms are a problem because President Ruto is a 'softy Christian' ('mkiristo'), blaming democratic rights ('ufala' — foolishness/chaos) on his religious identity — a low-level religiously tinged political insult.

terms: You will do nothing about it
exp: 'TUTAM' (likely acronym for a threatening phrase against Ruto) paired with 'you will do nothing about it' constitutes an explicit threat against a named individual (the president), elevated beyond mere insult.

'Zomalis' (derogatory respelling of Somalis) are collectively portrayed as anti-democratic chaos-bringers who 'can't govern themselves' and have damaged Kenya, Europe and America — a dehumanising collective-blame stereotype with an implicit exclusion demand.
Near-identical to post 3 — political criticism of 'RiggyG' as a 'Tribal Clown/#TribalMerchant' framed around institutional democracy; sharp political insult with ethnic labelling but no incitement.
Calls a named individual ('Kasongo') 'ng'ombe' (cow/idiot) and accuses him of corruption — personal insult and character attack on a specific individual with no group-identity dimension.

A neutral, surprised observation that Luos and Luhyas are fighting, attributing it to politics ('siaga') — no slur, no incitement, no hate; this is commentary on inter-ethnic political tension, not hate speech.
Post uses 'easy minded bantus' as a derogatory ethnic stereotype while making a geographic argument about African security, constituting baseline ethnic insult.

Though the target group is not named explicitly, the post labels an unnamed 'these people' as terrorists, mutilators and every evil, dehumanising them and issuing an implicit incitement to punish them or face enslavement — meeting multiple Benesch dangerous-speech markers.

Post explicitly calls for war against Islam and urges readers to arm themselves, framing Christian–Muslim coexistence as impossible — a direct incitement to religiously motivated violence meeting the Rabat threshold.
Swahili comment ('human rights people will cause trouble') is a cynical remark about human-rights advocates in a law-enforcement context, not identity-based hate speech.

terms: ancestral lineage is not one of them
exp: 'Jaluo' (Luo ethnic label used pejoratively) is called 'mjinga' (fool/idiot) and then told their ancestral lineage does not belong in Kenya, combining ethnic insult with an exclusion demand.
Post dismisses a named woman as 'clueless' solely on the basis of her gender while telling her to read the constitution, constituting a gendered insult.

Post criticises Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua ('RiggyG') as a 'Tribal Clown' and '#TribalMerchant' — political criticism of a named official's ethnic politics rather than an attack on an identity group.

Swahili post reflects on the death of someone labelled a criminal ('jambazi'/bandit) and the social customs around mourning criminals — commentary on crime and society, not identity-based hate speech.

Post labels 'Zionists' as 'servants of Satan' running a 'satanic empire' — religious/political dehumanisation — while calling a multi-faith coalition to 'fight against' them, constituting dangerous speech with dehumanisation and accusation-mirror markers.

Post commemorates the 1957 hanging of Kenyan freedom fighter Dedan Kimathi and uses strong derogatory language ('looters, rapists, murderers, thieves') toward colonial British forces — anti-colonial historical commentary that borders on group insult toward a national group.
'Wahehe' is used here as a derogatory label for a group accused of delaying national progress, applying an ethnic slur to dismiss political opponents.

Radical political rhetoric framing Kenya as a colonial plantation and implying dialogue is useless, calling for street action — political criticism with provocative but non-specific language, borderline incitement without a concrete call to violence.
Mocks a religious community (implied conservative Muslims debating dress codes) as 'filled with stupidity' for rejecting modern clothing while benefiting from modern technology.

Arabic post stating 'whoever destabilises stability deserves what comes to them, his sin is on his side' — ambiguous political warning that could justify harm against dissidents but lacks a specific target or identity attack.
Calls a political leader a 'black colonial', 'senge' (derogatory for a promiscuous woman/worthless person), and 'garbage', combining gendered and political insults against a named individual.

Calls President Ruto a 'murderer' and labels another named individual 'totally stupid' (Jinga kabisa) in the context of political criticism of a human-rights compensation panel — political insult of named individuals rather than identity-group hate.

Blanket claim that every Muslim nation, community and mosque wants to destroy America, framing Islam as an existential totalitarian threat — collective dehumanisation with an existential-threat Benesch marker against the entire Muslim religious group.
Attributes a murder accusation against a named individual (Uhuru) to the entire Kikuyu ethnic group with the collective label 'killers', constituting ethnic dehumanisation via collective guilt.

Repeatedly labels a named political figure (Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua) a 'Tribal Clown' and 'Tribal Merchant', political insults targeting an individual's conduct rather than attacking an identity group.

Somali-language post describes southern Somalia (Koonfurta) as full of terrorist groups, spies of foreign states, and Arab-aligned actors, and implies Somaliland cannot negotiate with such people — political commentary with derogatory framing of southern political actors but no group-identity hate attack.
'Reer Xareed' (lineage/clan of Xareed) is mocked with the slur that their legs are small/weak and bullets fall off them — a dehumanising taunt against a specific clan lineage presented as a joke.

The post asks whether Bashiir Amaan's new political party is like that of jihadist Aadan Xaashi Cayrow, accusing him of promoting jihad and flying the black (ISIS-style) flag — political attack on an individual using extremist association, not a group hate attack.

'Indr' is an abbreviated form of 'inader/idoor' (anti-Isaaq clan slur), directed at Cirro, accusing him of having no genuine interest in Somaliland and wanting to insult other clans (reer kale) — clan-coded insult targeting a political individual.
The post calls a named account 'Tuug' (thief) and 'caqli digaag' (chicken-brained/stupid) and dismisses them — personal insult directed at an individual Twitter user.
Brief reply calling a named account a thief ('tuug') in agreement with another user — baseline personal insult.

Post complains that foreign actors ('shisheeye' — foreigners/outsiders) are always present behind the walls in tents, sarcastically questioning the legitimacy of a one-man-one-vote process — political criticism with anti-foreigner framing but no clear group-hate target.

Post labels former president Muuse Bihi 'Muuse Tuug' (Muuse the thief), accusing him of plunging the country into war and stealing/embezzling 150 million, and contrasts him with Cirro as the rightful president — personal political insult targeting a named individual.

terms: reerkodii Yara ba mindiyaha loo afeystay
exp: Post mocks WHO Director-General Tedros Ghebreyesus, calling him 'Tigre' (ethnic slur for Tigrayan) with 'mayal adag' (stubborn/arrogant mule) and alludes to his family members being 'given to the knife' (killed), using ethnic identity to dehumanise and gloat over Tigrayan suffering during the Ethiopian conflict.

'Tuug la shaqeysta cadowga' means 'thief working with the enemy' — the post labels Turkey a collaborating enemy and demands its withdrawal from Somalia, which is political criticism with a borderline insult rather than clear identity-based hate speech.

'Bantu' is used here neutrally/descriptively (not as the slur 'jareer') to identify victims of Hemedti's RSF massacres — the post condemns atrocities against Sudanese civilians and is counter-speech/condemnation rather than hate speech.

The post dehumanises the target as 'filthy bastards' and 'origin of all sinners,' invokes Abu Lahab (a Quranic archetype of damnation) to religiously condemn a Muslim refugee, and demands they 'go back to Saudi,' combining religious vilification with exclusion demand.

The post makes pop-culture character comparisons (Jujutsu Kaisen) using 'murtad' (apostate) as a descriptor in a casual, apparently satirical context — borderline low-level religious stereotyping but arguably not targeted hate speech; not East Africa-relevant.
'Kafir' (infidel) is used to disparage non-Muslim K-pop/East Asian culture and shame Muslims who engage with it — intra-religious shaming with a religious slur, not East Africa-specific.

'Murtad fauj' labels the Pakistani army as apostate soldiers; glorifying an 'Allah-accepted sacrifice' against them frames lethal violence as religiously sanctioned martyrdom — not East Africa-specific but coded incitement glorification.
'Kafiro' (infidels) is used to accuse Pakistan/Afghanistan of siding with non-believers while fighting each other — a religious slur in a geopolitical commentary, not East Africa-relevant.
'Jareer' is an anti-Bantu/African racial slur used by some Somalis; here it derogatorily stereotypes a Black person as a poor Section 8 resident, constituting ethnic-racial insult.
'Jareer' (lit. 'hard hair,' anti-Bantu slur) is hurled as a straightforward racial insult at the addressee.

'Dirty Jareer' and 'Bantu' are used as racial slurs to dehumanise Bantu/African women by sexualising and degrading them, while 'honorable Somali mother' constructs an explicit ethnic hierarchy — combining anti-Bantu dehumanisation with gendered sexual degradation.
User asks what 'jareer' (anti-Bantu/hard-hair racial slur) means, framed as a question rather than a direct attack, making it borderline rather than clearly hateful.
Single-word reply calling an individual an apostate ('murtad'), a religiously loaded slur that carries serious stigma in Somali/Islamic contexts.
Post uses 'jareer' (anti-Bantu slur) to question someone's Somali identity and pairs ableist language with a moral accusation of disgracing Muslim men, combining ethnic and religious insult.
Dismisses a user's opinion by labelling them an apostate ('murtad detected, opinion rejected'), using religious slur to delegitimise rather than engage.
Uses 'jareer' (anti-Bantu racial slur) and 'wasaq' (dirty/filth insult) to demean a person on ethnic grounds and mock their right to speak on citizenship matters.
Academic/genealogical discussion of haplogroup lineages among Somali caste minorities (Madhiban/Midgan, Tumal) and Oromo analogues; no hateful intent detected.
User clarifies a factual genealogical claim about Mo Farah's caste/clan background (Madhiban) without derogatory framing; descriptive not hateful.
Flatly denies a person Somali identity on ethnic grounds using the anti-Bantu slur 'jareer', performing ethnic exclusion — a Benesch exclusion-demand marker.
French-language post calls the addressee an infidel ('kafir') in response to a comment about age/content, deploying a religious slur to dismiss and stigmatise.
Labels interlocutors' rabbis as 'murtad' (apostates) guilty of apostasy and treason, using a religious slur to delegitimise and stigmatise in an inter-faith dispute.
The post uses 'jareer' (racial slur for Somali Bantu/hard-hair people) to dismiss a Somali word as belonging to an inferior ethnic group, implying Bantu Somalis' language is foreign or lesser.
The post uses 'jareer' as a slur to mock Somali Bantu people who claim land, dismissing them as associated with a failed state and unworthy of respect.

'Najis' means ritually impure/filth in Arabic/Islamic context, and 'mugholadzoh' appears to be a derogatory Indonesian/Malay term; the post is an insult but lacks sufficient context to confirm a clear East African hate-speech target.
The post deploys 'jareer' (anti-Bantu racial slur) as a direct insult against an individual in a dispute about Islam's image.
The post combines a body-shaming insult ('fat') with the racial slur 'jareer' to demean a specific individual on ethnic grounds.
The post uses 'jareer' as a derogatory ethnic label applied to a football club, mocking its association with Somali Bantu people.
The post combines body-shaming ('fat') with the racial slur 'jareer' to demean an individual on ethnic grounds.
The post uses 'jareer' to stereotype Somali Bantu people as intellectually inferior, implying only they would post something foolish.
The post self-identifies as 'kafir' (infidel) and attacks Islam by mocking the Kaaba and insulting the Prophet as a 'pedophile warlord', constituting anti-Muslim hate speech.

'Khaayin' means traitor in Somali; the post accuses a specific individual of being a traitor working for enemies and questions their Somali identity, constituting targeted political-identity abuse directed at one person.

The post challenges another user's Islamic credentials by asking if they are an apostate ('murtad'), using a slur-adjacent term in a theological dispute rather than a clear identity attack on a group.
The post (Indonesian/Malay: 'The best thing is to be an apostate') uses 'murtad' approvingly to mock or dismiss Islam, constituting an insult directed at Muslim identity in a Somali-tagged context.

The post attacks unnamed Somali users as 'closet apostates' (murtads) hiding behind nationalism, and insults the target as a 'laangaab' (short-lineage/low-clan minority slur), combining religious and clan-hierarchy abuse.

The post uses 'cagdheer' (anti-Darod/Ogaden clan slur) and 'jareer' (dehumanising racial slur for Somali Bantu, meaning 'hard hair') to demean a specific user, ordering them to 'know your place as a jareer foot soldier,' combining ethnic dehumanisation with an exclusion demand.

The post uses 'Bantu' as a racial pejorative to denigrate southern Somalis as genetically inferior/mixed, while elevating Amhara/Habesha ancestry, constituting ethnic-based insult and racist hierarchy.

The post uses 'gaalo' (infidels/non-believers) mockingly twice — taunting a Somali user that non-Muslims are protesting in their capital and are the only reason Somalia exists as a country, deploying the slur derisively rather than as direct incitement.
The post sarcastically suggests that 'gaalo' (infidels) will have to protect the target's women and children, using the slur to shame the opponent while implicitly invoking gendered dishonour tropes.
The post shames the target by implying their daughters are with 'gaalo' (infidels) in their own homes, using the slur to attack religious and gendered honour simultaneously.
The post uses 'Bantu' as a reductive ethnic insult, rhetorically claiming Somalia is a 'Bantu country' as a pejorative jab likely in a lineage/identity dispute.

The post accuses Somalis of pandering to 'gaalo' (infidels/non-Muslims) by spreading propaganda against fellow Somalis, using the slur to shame intra-community criticism as collaboration with outsiders.

Post uses 'jareer' (anti-Bantu racial slur meaning 'hard hair') alongside repeated primate comparisons ('monkey blood', 'part monkey') to dehumanise Nigerians and implicitly Somali Bantus while asserting Somali racial superiority.

Post calls an unnamed person a 'murtad' (apostate — a serious religious slur in Islamic contexts) and 'neoliberal missionary' in a political-religious polemic referencing October 7th and anti-colonialism rhetoric.

Post makes pseudo-anthropological claims about southern Somalis having 'Bantu admixture' with an implicit hierarchy favouring 'pure Somalis', reproducing anti-Bantu/jareer ethnic prejudice in physical-appearance framing.

Post defends the slur 'jareer' as a neutral identity label while acknowledging Somalis are also named by others, minimising rather than deploying the slur offensively — but the normalisation of a derogatory term still constitutes baseline insult content.
Post uses 'meedi jareer' (combining a derogatory Somali term for mixed/inferior with the anti-Bantu racial slur 'jareer/hard-hair') as a dismissive insult directed at a named individual.

Post groups the UK and Netanyahu together and uses 'gaalo' (infidels/non-believers) to mock the distinction between 'good infidels and bad infidels', deploying a religious slur against Western/Israeli political actors.
'Najis' (ritually impure in Arabic/Islamic fiqh) posted in isolation with no identifiable target, context, or group, making classification as hate speech impossible.

Swahili-language post explicitly states preference for 'Somalis from Somalia' over 'jareer' (anti-Bantu slur for Somali Bantus/Black Africans), reproducing ethnic hierarchy and racial othering within the Somali community.
'Najis' posted in isolation with no target or context — cannot be coded as hate speech without a discernible target group or individual.

Post uses Islamic purity terms 'najis' (ritually impure) and 'haram' (forbidden) directed at a user handle with no identifiable target group or hate-speech content beyond a personal insult without group dimension.
Calls the individual an infidel ('kafir') and warns of divine punishment, framing them as outside the faith community.
Labels a group as apostates ('murtad') and hypocrites ('munafiq'), stripping them of Muslim identity as an insult.
Declares that an apostate ('murtad') cannot be Iranian, using religious labelling to deny national belonging and exclude.
Anti-Islam post claiming Muslims lose intelligence upon conversion, insulting the Prophet Muhammad and the faith broadly.
Derides the Quran and Hadith as a 'trash religion mess', constituting blanket anti-Islamic abuse.
Promotes a binary 'Muslim or kafir (infidel)' framing that denies moderate/liberal Muslim identities and implicitly excludes them from the community.
Uses the caste slur 'midgaan' (Madhiban/Gabooye hereditary minority) combined with 'munaafiq' (hypocrite) and a '68 IQ' dehumanising stereotype to denigrate a community criticising a woman.
Labels Pakistan as apostate ('murtad') in a geopolitical comment about GDI pressure and ISIS, using a religious slur to delegitimise a state.

Uses Somali clan slurs — 'qadadwyn' (anti-Darod derogatory), 'faqash' (Barre-regime collaborator insult), and 'laandheere/laangaab' (short-lineage/inferior minority slur) — to mock a speaker and those he allegedly manipulates across clan lines.
Calls a diaspora Somali the greatest 'laangaab' (short/inferior lineage slur) ever, mocking his refugee background and questioning his religious and cultural authenticity compared to Somalilanders.
Claims the Hawiye clan are Bantu (a racial exclusion slur in Somali context implying non-Somali/non-Cushitic inferiority), denying their Somali identity and ethnically othering them.
Racially degrades the Darod clan by calling them 'Bantu Oromo minority' (denying Somali identity), adds dehumanising animal slur 'dirty rat', and demands they stop claiming Somali ethnicity.
'Essa beesha so fala abobora' targets the Issa clan (beesha = community/clan) with 'abobora' (pumpkin-head, a derogatory insult), a low-level clan slur.
Directs two slurs at a named Kenyan politician Aden Duale: 'jareer' (racial slur for hard-haired/Bantu-descent people) and 'kafir' (infidel/non-believer), combining ethnic and religious abuse.
Hurls racial slur 'jareer' at a named individual, mocks their physical appearance, and issues an explicit implicit threat ('your days are numbered'), constituting a targeted personal threat.

Uses the term 'kafir' (infidel) but the post appears to be questioning or criticising the concept of respecting non-Muslims rather than inciting against them; context is ambiguous but leans toward religious gatekeeping commentary rather than direct hate.

Combines 'jareer' (Bantu racial slur) with 'chimpanzee' (primate dehumanisation) against a Kenyan user and tells them Kenya is not their country, stacking ethnic dehumanisation with national exclusion.
Self-aware use of 'jareer' (racial slur for Bantu-descent/hard-hair) to express prejudiced irritation toward an unnamed person perceived as such; casual racism at low severity.
'Gaboye' is a Somali hereditary caste minority group name used here as a slur combined with 'boonk' (a derogatory insult), targeting a user with caste-based abuse.

Attacks a woman's PhD credentials and modesty (cowrada = nakedness/lack of modesty), calling her behaviour equivalent to 'gaalo' (infidels/non-Muslims), combining religious insult with gender-based shaming.
The user asks if 'jareer' (anti-Bantu racial slur meaning 'hard/kinky hair') means 'gay', trivialising the slur while still deploying it as a pejorative label.
The post calls Kenyan authorities 'gaalo' (infidels/unbelievers) and frames Kenya's presence in the NFD as occupation, implicitly demanding liberation of Somalis from non-Muslim rule.
'Jareer' (anti-Bantu racial slur) is used as a derogatory label combined with 'krinj' (cringe) to mock and demean the target based on ethnicity.
The post uses 'jareer brain' (invoking the anti-Bantu racial slur) to insult the target's intelligence in a theological argument about Muslim prayer practices.
The post labels someone a 'murtad' (apostate) by analogy, applying the concept to Hinduism; while brief, it uses a religiously charged slur implying condemnation of someone who has left their faith.
Written in Malay/Indonesian, the post taunts a former Muslim as 'murtad' (apostate) and 'kapir/kafir' (infidel), mocking them for commenting on Islam after leaving it — not East Africa-related.

The post sarcastically engages with a user whose handle includes 'Kafir' (infidel), challenging them to deny Islam's truth — anti-religious provocation but directed at a self-labelled account with no group incitement.
The post mocks a user (handle 'Pakistani_Kafir' = infidel) for alleged psychological fear of Islam, engaging in inter-religious taunting with no group-level incitement and no East Africa nexus.
A brief but blunt derogatory post using the anti-Bantu racial slur 'jareer' combined with 'fucking dumb' to demean someone on ethnic grounds.

The post uses 'jareer' (anti-Bantu slur) and 'babatunde' (stereotyped Nigerian name used dismissively) to demean a Nigerian interlocutor while making condescending claims about Nigeria's religious future and language.

The post uses a debunked IQ statistic to frame Somalis as cognitively deficient ('borderline retarded'), dehumanising an entire ethnic/national group while falsely claiming the framing is scientific rather than racist.
The post makes a benign physical-resemblance observation about a named individual; no hate speech, slur, or identity-based attack is present.

exp: Written in Juba Arabic, the post characterises the community (implicitly Nuer, given geographic context of Nasir/Baliet) as 'a society built on looting and lying', a collective ethnic stereotype, while ostensibly calling for peace.

The post uses the phrase 'Somali fraud' to collectively attribute criminal behaviour to an entire ethnic/national group, functioning as an ethnic stereotype and group libel.

The post discusses internal Somali clan politics involving Cidagale, Reer Guleid, Reer Haroun and Ogadeen sub-groups in the context of a 2006 incident and requests for asylum/protection, functioning primarily as clan political commentary rather than overt hate speech, though clan framing carries identity-conflict risk.

The post is a humorous Swahili anecdote about how the author would react nervously to a Russian accent on the street given the Russia-Ukraine war context; it contains no hate speech, slurs or identity attacks.

In Somali, the post says 'Hamse wants to step out of his role — the old Hassan-era man has been jumped/replaced', referencing political figures Hamse and Hassan (likely Somali political leaders) in a mocking tone, which is political commentary rather than group-identity hate speech.

'Laandheere' is a lineage reference used mockingly and 'laangaabtu' (short-lineage/low-status minority slur) is applied to insult a named teacher, dismissing him as not a real clan member ('Qabiil maaha').

The post singles out the Madhibaan (a Somali hereditary occupational caste/minority group) by name, framing their 'sweet-voiced' support as now cursed, implying divine retribution is falling on them and rhetorically questioning whether they will mourn or keep talking — an accusation-mirror and existential-threat framing against a caste group.

'Eelay' refers to a Somali occupational caste minority (sab); the post questions whether the Eelay, even if they ally with the government, could remove someone from office — a dismissive, low-status framing of a caste group's political agency.
The post mocks a Dhulbahante (Darod sub-clan) woman as ugly ('fool xun'), combining clan-based and gender-based insult.
'Laandheere' (lineage slur for low-status) is mocked for seeking justice while a 'Habarjaclo' (Isaaq sub-clan) elder is disparaged, and youth are accused of blindly following one clan side.

'Faqashta' (slur for Siad Barre-era regime loyalists) is used to accuse Raxanweyn (Digil-Mirifle clan) members of reviving 1991-era atrocities — dragging a farmer's body — framing a clan group as perpetrators of historical brutality (dehumanisation and accusation-mirror).

The post criticises a named individual for tolerating humiliation inflicted by states it calls Somalia's enemies — political criticism of a figure's stance, with no identity-group slur or dehumanisation.

The post expresses ethnically motivated voting intent ('my Luo Nation') and implicitly dismisses Rift Valley/Mt. Kenya (Kalenjin/Kikuyu) political dominance — political tribalism but at low severity with no dehumanisation or slur.

The post jokes that President Deni, upon seeing a photo, would curse ('nacallaa') the Hawiye clan and flee back to Garowe — a mocking, clan-baiting insult framing Hawiye as threatening to a Darod/Majeerteen figure.
The post poses a rhetorical question about military-minded people asking when they will act — general political frustration with no identity-group targeting, slur, or dehumanisation.

'Gurguurte' (a named individual, likely a political figure) is accused of seizing the country by military force and will cause a civil war ending in his downfall — an incitement framing him as an existential threat to the state.
Post claims Turkey and Saudi Arabia want a military base at Laasqoray and accuses Turkey of bringing 'new colonialism' — political criticism of foreign interference without identity-based hate.

The post calls a sweeping list of religious and political groups (Jews/Zionists, Freemasons, Wahhabis, etc.) 'ANIMALS', dehumanising multiple identity groups in a conspiracy-framing hashtag pile-on, with a Somali-country tag anchoring it to the dataset.

'Idoor' (anti-Isaaq slur) and 'Wagaash' are used as clan insults; a person advocating Majeerteen reconciliation with Isaaq is called a 'daanyeer' (monkey/ape — dehumanising), and the post claims the Dhulbahante clan already defeated/broke the Idoor, framing inter-clan rivalry with dehumanisation and implicit exclusion.

Post mocks Isaaq clan members for hollow status-seeking ('gob' = nobility used sarcastically) and calls them 'doqmo hanfade' (stupid arrogant fools), also dismissing women who marry into the clan as unfit for leadership — combining clan insult with gender-based dismissal.
The post criticises a named individual (@barre252) as blinded by 'qabyaalad' (clannism/tribalism) and unfit to be a politician — political personal criticism without a group-identity hate target.

The post rebukes a specific user (@hargeisa234) as hypocritical and ignorant, using insults like 'doqon' (idiot) and accusing him of clannism ('qabyaalad'), but the attack is on an individual rather than a group.

'Laangaab' (short-lineage slur for minority/low-status clan) is called resentful and cowardly, accused of fleeing after committing clan massacres ('xasuuqa') and dying disgracefully in a Nigerian toilet — dehumanising language targeting a minority clan group.

The post uses 'gaalada' (infidels) as a derogatory label for DP World supporters alongside a crude sexual insult ('futada hooyadaa' — your mother's genitals'), combining religious slurring with personal abuse in a political dispute.

'Qudhunkani' (this filthy/disgusting one) is used to demean a person accused of not truly belonging to the country and treating citizens as enemies — xenophobic/othering insult targeting someone's legitimacy as a national.

The post calls a named individual a 'slave' (Cabiid), an anti-Isaaq slur (iidoor), a 'short-lineage/lesser clan' slur (laangaab), and invokes God's curse on them in a territorial dispute over Somaliland.

The post uses the clan-hierarchy slur 'laangaab' against a named individual, then dehumanises all Somalis (southern Somalia) by comparing them unfavourably to apes, constituting dehumanisation under the Benesch framework.

The post dismisses the addressee and his elder associates, blaming 'the infidels/unbelievers' (gaalada) for destroying the country, using a religious slur to assign collective blame.

The post is a sustained torrent of gender-based abuse targeting a specific Somali woman, calling her a 'whore' (dhillo), 'cheap cooking-fat/worthless' (Bidco), 'idiot' (nacas), 'shameful/forbidden disgrace' (Xaaraan ceeb), 'enemy' (Cadow) and 'thief' (Tuug), apparently attacking her for marrying outside the community in the US.

The post uses the clan-inferiority slur 'laangaab' combined with an antisemitic trope, asserting the speaker's group are not slaves to 'the Jews', linking clan pride to anti-Jewish sentiment.
The post is a short, playful/teasing comment ('remove the enemy you see') directed at a specific Twitter user with laughing emojis, lacking any hate-speech content or group targeting.

Labels named Somaliland political figures Muse Bihi and Cirro as 'Faqash' (Barre-regime loyalist slur), delegitimising both as regime collaborators.

A brief political statement labelling adversaries 'Zionists' and 'Wahhabi terrorists' — primarily political/religious slur use in a conflict framing context, with no direct East Africa target and no incitement.

'Mushrik' (polytheist/idolater) is used as a religious slur in what appears to be a fragmented insult directed at someone's faith, though the full context is unclear.

This is a factual conflict-mapping summary describing the militia alignments and ethnic dimensions of the Upper Nile fighting, constituting journalistic/analytical content rather than hate speech.

Swahili post sarcastically mocking police ('POLICCM') and East African authorities for offering forgiveness without accountability — political satire/criticism, not identity-based hate speech.

Post mocks men of the Tulo Guled and Daari (sub-clan) lineages in Somali, calling them weak/subordinate ('landheraysanaa' — being overshadowed/dominated) and invoking a curse ('Nacalaa'), targeting specific clan groupings with ridicule.

Post uses 'caddaan' (white person) and mocks Somalis ('Soomaalida') by sarcastically asking why a white man speaks down to them ('u caayayaa' — barks at/belittles), delivering a low-level ethnic jibe with a laughing tone.

Post attacks someone referred to as 'Masiixu Dijaal' (the Christian/Antichrist — a religious slur framing a Christian as the Dajjal/false messiah), accusing them of daily fabrications against Islam and the country, constituting religious insult and delegitimisation.

Post insults named individual Faarax Macallin as intellectually deficient and full of hatred ('garasho liita, nacayb'), comparing him to someone shouting in a public gathering place ('marfash'), and accuses him of pushing extremism ('aragagixisonimo') on Kenyan social media.

Post calls named individual Xilibaan Dhashane 'Qashinkii' (garbage/trash) and associates him with Donald Trump's rhetoric, then turns the insult back on the reader, constituting personal abuse of a named individual.

Post constructs an equivalence chain ('anti-Somali = state-seeker, anti-state = clan-seeker') that frames clan loyalty as antithetical to nationhood and implicitly demands exclusion of clan-oriented actors, a Benesch accusation-mirror and exclusion-demand against clan identity in Kenya's Somali context.

Post dismisses criticism of President HSM (Hassan Sheikh Mohamud) as jealousy ('Xaasidnimo') by angry Hawiye clan members, deploying clan labelling ('Hawiya') to delegitimise political opposition as clan-driven spite.

Post uses 'faqash' (slur for Barre-regime/Darood loyalists) and 'xayawaan' (animal/beast) to dehumanise the targeted clan group, while framing their hostility as justifying reciprocal hatred — a Benesch accusation-mirror combined with dehumanisation.

Post uses 'Qadaad weyn' (a major anti-Darod/Ogaden derogatory slur) alongside 'foolxumo' (ugliness) and 'caqli xumo' (stupidity) to dehumanise the targeted clan group with compounded slurs, constituting dehumanising hate speech.

Post gossips about a domestic dispute between two named individuals (Fahiima and Firdhiso) and makes a mild disparaging remark about 'MJ' (Majeerteen clan), but is primarily personal drama/commentary rather than group-targeted hate.

Post alleges Somalia and Djibouti paid to track Somaliland president Cirro's location and accuses him of 'ethnic hatred' (isir Necayb) and slander (Af lagaado), functioning primarily as political criticism of a named leader.
Post calls Somalis 'qashin' (garbage/trash) and claims they have no functioning state or army — a derogatory ethnic-national slur targeting Somalis as a people.

Post describes a clan leader (Xawaadle/Reer Siciid lineage) withdrawing from a media outlet over a dispute with named individuals, framed as intra-clan political commentary without explicit slurs or calls to violence.
Post uses 'hablihiina' (your women) and 'Fiqiyoow' (clan/lineage address) in a sexualised taunt linking women of the group to AMISOM soldiers, constituting gendered clan-targeted insult.

'Khartoumers' is a dismissive label for people associated with Khartoum (Sudan), used derogatorily in South Sudanese political discourse, but the post is too terse to confirm clear hate speech without further context.

Post references Mathiang Anyor (Dinka ethnic militia) fighters as now destitute and 'perfectly deranged,' which is contemptuous commentary on a Dinka-associated militia rather than a direct call to violence.
Post explicitly calls on opposition military wings to unite to 'fight the regime in Juba' before end of Q1 2026, constituting incitement to armed conflict against a political target.

Post uses 'Midgaan' (a deeply derogatory slur for Somali hereditary caste minorities) and attacks a Majeerteen woman married to a caste man, then stereotypes the Majeerteen clan as cowardly fighters who beg 'brother don't kill me' — combining caste dehumanisation with clan defamation.

Post calls the target a 'Yibir' (lowest-status Somali caste minority slur), 'cagdheer' (anti-Darod slur), 'axmaar' (donkey/fool), 'yahuuda' (Jew, used as slur), and 'adoon/anjaas' (slave), stacking caste, clan, religious and racial dehumanisation against a specific user.
'Xayawaan' means 'animal/beast' — the post dehumanises a named individual (@ToddSchoenberg) by calling him an animal while telling him to mind his own city's business.

'Midgaan' is a derogatory slur for a Somali hereditary-caste minority (Madhiban/Gabooye group), and 'yuhuuda' (Jews) is used as an additional insult, accusing the targeted person of selling themselves to Jews.

'Iidoor/Idoor' is an anti-Isaaq clan slur, 'Kacaan orphans' dismissively labels pro-union Somalis as remnants of the Barre regime, and 'Xaasidnimo' (jealousy/spite) frames unionist political activity as clan-driven malice against Somaliland.

The post criticises Muslims who perform takfir (declaring other Muslims infidels) and calls that behaviour 'ape behaviour,' combining a mild dehumanising slur with a religious target, likely in a Somali context.

'Rajiim' (accursed/devil-driven) is used to vilify a named Somali militia/faction leader accused of destroying his city, massacring civilians, and inviting Ethiopian troops into Mogadishu — harsh political abuse of a public figure without a direct incitement call.

The post targets Somali-owned daycares in Columbus, Ohio, framing them as venues for deception and 'propaganda,' using an accusation-mirror dynamic (falsely attributing bad-faith to Somali immigrants) that could mobilise community hostility against a diaspora ethnic minority.

The post frames Somalia as 'ungrateful' for U.S. aid and celebrates its permanent cut-off, using nationalist 'America First' rhetoric to stigmatise Somalis as undeserving foreigners — baseline xenophobic insult against a national/ethnic group.

'Nacas' (idiot/fool) and 'magafe' (a derogatory term for an unjust/predatory actor) are used to insult parties holding prisoner families hostage in Las Anod, framing them as callously extorting relatives — political abuse without a direct incitement call.

The post uses 'retarded' as a blanket slur against Somalis who undertake irregular migration (tahriib), combining ableist language with ethnic targeting while contextualising it within Libya's violence.

'Jieng' is the Dinka ethnic self-designation and 'Jiengism' is a coded term for perceived Dinka ethno-political supremacy in South Sudan — the post approvingly invokes Dinka ethnic solidarity and dominance as the unifying national identity, constituting ethnic-supremacist framing.

Generic pile of insults with no specific identity target named — likely directed at a South Sudanese ethnic group given context but no explicit group marker is used, making it questionable rather than confirmed hate speech.

'Adoon' (slave/enslaved-caste slur) and 'Eelaay' (a Somali caste/sab minority group) are used to demean and exclude the target, telling them to leave the space between Hawiye and Darod — combining caste dehumanisation with an exclusion demand.

Swahili 'wajinga' (fools/idiots) is used dismissively about Kenyans generally in the context of a cynical political/civic comment about diaspora engagement and AI — frustration rhetoric rather than targeted identity hate speech.

Somali 'kansarka' (cancer) applied metaphorically to Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, calling him a 'cancer of the Somali nation' and demanding his resignation — political insult directed at a named individual.

The post criticises a young man from the Mareexaan (Somali clan) for seeking views and being driven by spite ('cuqdad'), calling him a coward ('gun gun dhashay') born of enemies ('cadow') — clan-based insult and character attack.

The post labels Somaliland's Isaaq-dominated administration as 'Isaaqland,' a secessionist entity, terrorist ('Argagixisada'), anti-Somali ('somalidiidka'), and apostate ('Murtadka') — stacking clan, religious and political slurs to delegitimise and dehumanise the entity and its leadership in the context of conflict with Djibouti.

Mixes what appears to be Oromo or another Horn language with Arabic Quranic verse (5:82) about Jews and polytheists ('Mushrikiin') being the greatest enemies of believers — framing non-Muslims as existential enemies of Islam and citing scripture to reinforce religious othering.

The post criticises a pro-Somaliland Islamic group ('kooxdii ictisaam') for internal divisions over how to conduct jihad regarding a contract dispute, and disparages Sufi supporters — internal Islamist political critique with religious framing but no direct incitement or clear slur target.

Accuses Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of planning to exploit Dhulbahante prisoners in Laascaanood to sow inter-clan enmity ('godob raagta') between the Isaaq and Dhulbahante clans — framing him as an agent of inter-clan manipulation, an accusation-mirror pattern stoking clan grievance.

'Laandheere' (tall/lanky — dismissive slur for a leader) and 'daba dhifka turkida' (Turkey's tail-follower/lackey) accuse Puntland leadership of subservience to Turkey and the UAE ('imaarad'), combining political insult with anti-foreign interference rhetoric.

'Cagdheer' is an anti-Darod clan slur; 'kalb ibnal kalb' means 'dog son of a dog' — the post dehumanises a named individual with a clan slur and directs them to protest at the Israeli embassy in Nairobi, implying they are a foreign collaborator and asserting Somaliland belongs to the speaker's clan.

'Jabanka' (lit. jawbone, used as a derisive clan/group insult), 'Daarood4' (clan reference), and 'iswarfiso' (exposing oneself/nude) are used to mock and sexually shame a woman associated with a rival clan group on social media.

'Xaaroods' is a derogatory corruption of 'Haroods/Daarood' used as a clan slur, and 'halgoodle' is a dismissive insult; the post asserts this clan has been effectively expelled from Mogadishu and are squatting on others' property, framing their presence as illegitimate.

The post asserts that anyone carrying a flag in Sanaag/Puntland should be arrested ('xarig' = rope/arrest), criticising the Sultan and local government as complicit in a political dispute over the region — primarily political criticism with an implicit threat of punishment framed as law.

'Qudhunka' (filth/rottenness) is used as an insult against what is framed as a dictator, and the post announces a military base will be given to 'Jabhadd canfarta' (an armed front) — this is political opposition rhetoric with mild abusive language rather than identity-based hate speech.

'Xiniyo salaaxa shisheeye' means roughly 'known for foreign/outsider testicle-licking' (a sexual-loyalty slur) and 'adoomo xambaari jiray' means 'slaves who served as porters' — the post dehumanises the Isaaq clan as colonial collaborators and slaves, contrasting them with a celebrated anti-colonial fighter.

terms: diverted billions to her home country
exp: The post targets a named Somali-origin U.S. political figure (implied to be Ilhan Omar), accusing her of corruption, terrorism financing, and looting America for Somalia — combining national-foreigner othering with an incitement-adjacent call to confiscate her assets and punish her.

The post makes a political argument against open-border immigration policy using Mogadishu as a rhetorical comparator — it is political commentary with nativist framing rather than direct identity-based hate speech, though it othering of migrants edges toward xenophobia.

'Reer Binu Israil' (children of Israel, used as a disparaging clan othering label) and 'gurguurte' (crawlers/creepers, a derisive slur) are used to mock President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, accusing him and his TikTok supporters of entering Sool illegally ('tahriib' = illegal migration).

The post stereotypes elderly Hawiye clan members as possessively nationalist ('laxaw' = greedy attachment to the country) while mocking Hawiye diaspora women ('qurba joog') as complainers and cursers — a clan-based insult contrasting homeland versus diaspora behaviour.

The post frames Somali immigrants in the USA as an economic burden and implicitly undesirable, using rhetorical questions to cast an ethnic/national group as a collective threat to national wealth — an exclusion-demand marker targeting Somalis as foreigners.

'OYOL MONEY' likely refers to communal/government funds associated with Nuer interests; the post is primarily mockery of corruption/embezzlement and uses Nuer identity as context rather than as a direct target of hatred, making it borderline political satire.

The post frames the Dinka ethnic group collectively as an instrument of a tyrannical regime, conflating an entire ethnicity with political oppression and poor governance — an accusation-mirror that risks casting Dinka as an existential obstacle to South Sudan's stability.

The post criticises Kenyans' alleged class-based selectivity in pursuing accountability against James Opande, implying hypocrisy rather than attacking a protected group — this is political/social commentary with mild generalisation rather than targeted hate speech.

In Somali, 'ajaanib' means foreigner/alien and 'afrikanka' is used dismissively; the post mocks a self-styled prime minister for having a foreign soldier with a runny nose ('sanka bagafsan') patrolling an airport of a country he claims — derogatory ridicule of a political figure using xenophobic framing.

'Xasaaniyiin' refers to Sufi/Qadiriyya followers of Sheikh Hassan; the post dismisses them as 'caqli yar' (few-minded/stupid), accuses them of takfir (declaring others infidels), and declares separation from them — a sectarian insult targeting a religious subgroup.

'Yahuudka' (the Jews) is invoked to argue that Israeli/Jewish connection benefits Somaliland's Awdal region commercially (Berbera port, northern opportunities), framing Jews instrumentally in geopolitical argument — borderline use of 'yahuud' as a derogatory shorthand but primarily political commentary rather than incitement.

The post dehumanises the Hawiye clan collective by labelling Mogadishu a 'genocidal ghetto' and 'Hawiye camp,' characterising Hawiye-associated actors as hooligans, thugs and criminals, while demanding complete exclusion of Somaliland from any relationship with them.

'Midgaan' is a derogatory slur for the Madhiban/Gabooye caste; 'leylkase' is an insult meaning worthless/destitute; 'qof qaawan' means naked/exposed person — the post publicly degrades a named individual by attacking their hereditary caste status and stripping them of dignity.

'Ey ey Dhalay' means 'born of a dog/dogs' (extreme dehumanisation); 'midgaan' is the hereditary caste slur; 'Uskag yahoow' means 'you filthy/stinky one' — the post combines animal-descent dehumanisation with caste slurring to maximally degrade the target.

The post uses 'Midgaan' (a derogatory caste slur for the Madhiban) to delegitimise Barkhad Batoon, accusing him of being a low-caste outsider who has no stake in the Isaaq–Dhulbahante conflict yet inflames it, invoking accusation-mirror logic (he's fanning a war his own people won't die in) and implicitly demanding his exclusion from political discourse.

'Midgaan maraxaan' combines the hereditary-caste slur with 'maraxaan' (worthless/pitiful) to shame and dismiss a named individual, telling them a boy knows better than them and to be ashamed before the elder.

The post accuses Djiboutian people of not needing a separatist clan ('qabiil gooni-u-goos') that is labelled 'Sahyuuniyiin' (Zionists), using the Zionist slur as a political-religious insult to delegitimise a diaspora/clan political movement.

The post calls Jibril Qoobey a 'miskin' (pitiful wretch) and a 'subcontract spy (basaaas) for the devil Arabs (UAE/Israel)', using religious-political insults to discredit him over DP World/Djibouti port politics.

The post mockingly nicknames a sheikh 'sh whisky' and lists Somali political/security figures, rhetorically asking who among them is not al-Shabaab — political sarcasm/insult directed at named officials rather than a protected identity group.

The post brands al-Shabaab as 'khawarij' (extremist apostates) and labels the Isaaq clan collectively as 'apostate Zionists' collaborating with Israel to seize Somali territory, constructing an existential-threat and accusation-mirror frame, then calls for Allah to 'DESTROY' both groups — a religious incitement to group violence meeting the Rabat threshold.

The post dehumanises Ethiopian migrants as people 'without morals/cleanliness' who bring diseases, using disease-contagion framing (a classic Benesch dehumanisation marker) to demand their exclusion from Puntland.

The post criticises a named individual for blocking the Awdal community ('reer awdal') from forming a political party and instead steering them toward 'Kaah' — borderline political grievance with mild clan framing but no overt slur or dehumanisation.

The post targets a named woman (@Sitti_Salal_Dji) with a gendered slur ('bitch'), mocks her praying for bullets ('rasaas ka baryee'), and threatens that a 'crawler/hitman' (gurgurrte) will catch up with her — constituting gendered harassment and an explicit personal threat.

The post criticises President Kiir's political decisions and mentions the Mathiang Anyor (Dinka ethnic militia) descriptively in a historical grievance context, with no identity attack — it is political commentary rather than hate speech.

The post publishes the full name, parents' names, place of birth, state, county, birthday, marital status and nationality of a named private individual, constituting doxxing that could enable targeting.
'Mundukuru' is a derogatory ethnic slur used in South Sudan (often against Equatorians or non-Nilotic groups), used here mockingly to celebrate a defeat.
The post condemns and reports an antisemitic slur used by Somalia's president against a visitor to Somaliland — this is counter-speech criticising a public official's hate, not hate speech itself.

The Somali-language post calls for those who have gathered to kill Somali people ('dadka somaliyeed dilaan') to themselves be shot dead ('ha la toogto dhanaantood') — an explicit incitement to lethal violence against a group.

The post describes the historical recruitment of the Dinka Mathiang Anyor militia before the 2013 civil war as a political grievance and lament for lives lost, functioning as critical commentary rather than hate speech.

'Kuar miidit' is a derogatory Dinka slur for Riek Machar; the post portrays Nuer White Army youth as disposable pawns destined to be 'completely wiped out' by the Red Belt and Mathiang Anyor, combining dehumanisation with an existential-threat framing that implicitly endorses the annihilation of Nuer fighters.

The post uses 'mkikuyu' (Kikuyu person) in a stereotyping context implying Kikuyu people are meat-eating beneficiaries of patronage networks, a low-level ethnic slur/stereotype targeting the Kikuyu community.

The post dismisses Kenyans and other nationals from 'third world countries' as irrelevant and associates Kenya with money laundering, constituting xenophobic insult directed at a national/foreigner group.

The post conflates all Somali people with fraud and al-Shabaab financing by labelling them 'Somalian fraudsters' and linking hawala transfers to terrorism, applying a collective criminal stereotype to a national/ethnic group.

The post mocks Madhiban people (a Somali caste group) by sarcastically questioning whether the 'Madhiban Garaad' (a titled elder among Madhiban) is truly of their lineage, telling them to 'lose their minds' — an insult directed at the Madhiban caste community.

The post calls on ICE and immigration authorities in the US, Canada, Australia, and Europe to specifically target and deport Somalis who identify as Madhiban (a stigmatised caste group), framing their caste identity as grounds for deportation and citing prior persecution in their home country as a pretext.

The post quotes a proverb about 'laangaab' (low/short-lineage, a slur for minority or caste groups) not being a clan matter but God-given, then appears to criticise a specific individual (a security guard at an embassy) — the coded term is cited to make a point rather than as a direct slur, making this borderline.

In Swahili, the post accuses someone of being a 'killer' who expels Tanzanian workers 'like dogs' (mbwa) daily and of having corrupted the CMA and courts — targeting Tanzanian nationals with a dehumanising animal comparison.

The post uses multiple derogatory clan-coded terms and insults ('gaylan'=loose woman, 'imaarad'=derogatory for Dhulbahante sub-clan, 'juxa/sintinow/hindia'=insults) directed against the Dhulbante clan and their leaders, while calling on others to unite against them.

The post calls the tagged individual (@FarahMaalimM) 'adoon' (slave) and claims he — born in Dadaab refugee camp — wants to destabilise a free, sovereign people so the camps become his source of livelihood, combining a dehumanising slave slur with anti-refugee othering.

The post accuses the tagged person of seeing the world with 'clan eyes' (indho reerood) and asks whether Egypt's presence in the Red Sea and Nile is an excuse to open doors to 'clan-state' recognition — political criticism using clan-bias framing, borderline insult rather than targeted hate.

The post alleges that no member of the Ciise clan has kidnapped or killed Gadabursi people, attributing violence instead to named political figure IOG and four allied clans, using accusation-mirror framing to cast the Ciise as victims and implicitly threatening reciprocal action.

The post criticises political attitudes around Laascaanood instability, calling opponents 'envious' and 'resentful' and questioning whether governance requires sitting in Mogadishu — political criticism with mild personal insults but no identity-based hate.

The post calls the tagged user a 'Midgan' (a deeply offensive slur for the Madhiban/Midgan caste group) and threatens that their land will be taken ('dhulkaagi lagu muransanyahay kasaar'), combining a caste slur with a territorial dispossession threat.
'Xayawaan' (animal) and 'xoolo' (livestock) dehumanise a person framed as Ethiopian ('Xabashaa u aabbo') or Kenyan, stripping them of humanity on ethnic/national grounds.

The post challenges Isaaq dominance in Somaliland by listing other groups including the Gaboye caste minority, implying Isaaq unfairly monopolise the state, with a mildly threatening prediction that Somalis will one day beg there.

The post singles out the Yibir (a marginalised Somali caste) and parts of Isaaq and labels them 'Bani Israel' (Jews), a coded conspiratorial othering that delegitimises their Somali identity and implicitly invokes antisemitic tropes.
'Qadaad' is an anti-Darod/anti-Harti slur and 'landers' dismisses Somaliland supporters; the post mocks the complainant and predicts the end of 'Greater Somalia', using clan-coded insults.

The post demands Turkey be expelled ('ha la saaro') and that the 'Frud Front' rebels based in Djibouti be given a military base in Somaliland, constituting an implicit call to support an armed faction against a foreign actor.

'Tahriib' (irregular migration) combined with 'Daacish' (ISIS) frames light-skinned ('Cadcad') migrants as ISIS soldiers, implying border closure is needed to stop jihadist infiltration — a dangerous conflation inciting exclusion of migrants on religious/national grounds.

'Islaan' is a gendered Somali insult (loose/disreputable woman) applied to President Hasan Sheikh to demean him via feminisation, while the post also dismisses Somali unity through clan framing of Darood vs. Hawiye.

'Camjiec' is an anti-Nuer ethnic slur in Nuer/South Sudanese context; the post calls on 'camjiec' (derogatory for Nuer) to stop polluting cattle camps with outsider cattle, using dehumanising in-group/out-group livestock framing that implicitly demands ethnic exclusion.

The post demeans Dhulbahante people under 'drunk/drugged Isaaq' soldiers and explicitly states they should have been shot ('in meesheda lagu toogto ayay ahayd'), constituting a call to lethal violence against a clan sub-group.

The post addresses Trump and uses the 'monkey with matches' metaphor to dehumanise and mock a named individual (Ali Arif), likely a Somali/East African political figure, as a reckless destructive actor.

'Madoadoa' (stains/outsiders) is invoked to frame Somali leaders and elders as foreign occupiers who displace locals and pit clans against each other, calling on God to destroy them — an incitement framing the target group as an existential threat to land and community.

The post targets a named individual (Hassan/Xasan) and a 'Djiboutian' (ina jabuutawi — son of a Djiboutian, used as a foreign-othering slur), threatening to imprison him ('waanu xidhno' — we will lock him up) if he is sent to them.

The post notes that Kisii people face ethnic discrimination ('ukabila'/tribalism) from other Kenyans, framing it more as an observation about prejudice than an attack, though it reproduces ethnic stereotyping about academic and immigration performance.
The post is a brief, apparently lighthearted or affectionate morning greeting referencing 'camba-luul' (a fruit/sweet) and a person named Muuse/Abbe — no hateful or abusive content detected.

The post accuses Hassan (likely Hassan Sheikh Mohamud) of seeking political chaos ('khakhal siyasadeed') in Somaliland regions and dismisses a short video of him in Laascaanood as the act of a 'permanent guest' ('doonyaa' used pejoratively) — primarily political criticism of a named leader without clear identity-group attack.

'Xaarood yaryar' (diminutive/derogatory for the Harti/Darood sub-clan) are branded enemies of Puntland and equated with followers of dictator Siad Barre ('afweyne'), with an incitement framing that they intend to destroy Puntland — a dangerous accusation-mirror narrative targeting a named clan.

'Reer hebel' (literally 'people of so-and-so clan', used as a coded placeholder to mock a specific clan without naming them) is used mockingly alongside laughing emojis, constituting mild clan-based ridicule; without the linked image/video context the full target is unclear.

'Midgaan' is a deeply derogatory slur for the Madhiban/Gabooye hereditary occupational caste in Somali society, weaponised here as a public insult against a specific individual (@LiBashe) to shame and socially demote them.

'Faqash' (slur for supporters of Siad Barre's regime, used as a political/clan insult) combined with 'xayawaan' (animal/beast — dehumanising) are directed at Hassan Sheikh Mohamud or his supporters, constituting dehumanising clan-political abuse.

The post hurls multiple personal insults at a specific user (@north_somalia), including 'xayawaan' (animal — dehumanising) alongside ableist slurs ('autistic', 'educationally sub-normal'), constituting targeted individual abuse rather than broad group incitement.
'Qadaad' is an anti-Darod/anti-Ogaden slur; the post directs it at a tagged individual, asking rhetorically whether she is 'a big qadaad' — a clan-based insult.

'Qadaad weyn ma ilbaxdo' (a big qadaad never civilises) is a clan slur against Darod/Ogaden, and 'xabaale qote' (grave-digger) is a derogatory insult aimed at President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, combining clan abuse with personal insult.

'Xaarood yaryar' is a derogatory diminutive of Harti/Darod and 'kurtun' is a vulgar insult, directed at a Majeerteen (Darod sub-clan) person in a personal online altercation involving a sexual slur about his mother.

'Tuugo' (thieves/bandits) is used as a clan-coded insult against a group the poster dismisses, while defending Somalilanders' political representation in the UK — borderline political but the slur makes it hateful.

'Munaafaqiin' (hypocrites — a religiously charged insult) is applied to named political figures Ordakhan and Al-Sisi, accusing them of secretly supporting Hamas, framing political opponents with religious-moral condemnation.

'Camjiɛc thielɛ wec' is a Dinka-language phrase using the anti-Nuer slur 'camjiɛc,' framing the Nuer as people who 'destroy/ruin the country,' which mirrors a grievance accusation against an ethnic group and carries a Benesch accusation-mirror marker.

'Faqash' (Barre-regime slur for certain Somalis/Darood), 'madoows' (racial slur for Black Africans, here targeting AMISOM troops), and 'ugandishu' (derogatory for Mogadishu) are combined with a call to expel foreigners and deny al-Shabaab adversaries legitimacy — amounting to incitement to exclude/expel.

'Bombdishu' and 'Ugandishu' are derogatory nicknames for Mogadishu used to mock the Somali federal government and a named individual (Roberto), dismissing Somalia's legitimacy in favour of Puntland — primarily political insult.

The post addresses Nuer White Army youth, warning them their armed mobilisation is futile against the SSPDF; while framed as a peace appeal, it implicitly frames Nuer armed resistance as an existential dead-end — a Benesch existential-threat framing — making it questionable rather than straightforwardly hateful.

This is a lyrical/poetic post referencing Somali artists (Hibo Maxamed Huddoon, Omar Dhuulle, Ali Sheekh) and their music — 'dhuulle' is an artist surname, not a slur — the post contains no hate speech.
Luganda-language phrase ('Mwenda wa bawanda na basimbi') is a proverb/saying with no hate-speech content directed at any group.

The post labels a community ('Arin Tani') as 'mushrikiin' (polytheists) who have 'become infidels/kuffar' (gaaloowdaye) and asserts there is therefore no Islamic legal standing (dacwad) for them — implicitly excluding them from Muslim community protections.

The post refers to a male group ('ragaas dhoobleey') as nomadic vagrants who have brought 'bahallo' (wild animals/beasts) into their territory ('galleenka'), dehumanising a clan-linked community by equating them with animals, and urges ignoring their grievances.

The post insults a named individual ('shiine culay') as a 'bahaluul' (fool/beast), accusing him of hiding behind 'qabiil' (clan) language and suggesting his clan/family needs to discipline him — clan-tinged personal abuse.

The post insults an individual as 'sarqaanow' (a thief/corrupt one), accuses him of clan ('qabiil') bias, and smears him as a 'yahuud family' (Jewish-linked, used as a slur) or anti-Somali, combining sectarian and clan-based abuse.
